title: Excretory urography (kidney X-ray with contrast)
what: A contrast dye is given into a vein and several X-rays are taken. They show how the kidneys pass urine and how it flows through the urinary tract.
why: For stones, lower back pain, blood in the urine and kidney abnormalities, when the doctor chooses this method.
duration: usually 30 to 60 minutes, sometimes longer; the report is ready the same day
tell_doctor: If you are allergic to iodine or contrast dye
If you have kidney disease, diabetes or thyroid disease
If you take diabetes medicines - your doctor will tell you what to do
If you might be pregnant or are breastfeeding

prepare.title: Test
prepare.text: A blood test for creatinine is often needed before the exam. Ask the clinic.

prepare.title: Bowel
prepare.text: Sometimes you are advised to have a light dinner the evening before and avoid foods that cause gas.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food in the morning. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. If you take diabetes medicines, ask your doctor in advance.

steps: You lie down on the X-ray table
A first picture is taken without contrast
Contrast is given into a vein
After a few minutes a series of pictures is taken
Sometimes you are asked to use the toilet and one more picture is taken
feel: When the contrast goes in - warmth through your body and a metallic taste in your mouth
Sometimes it feels like you need the toilet - this is the feeling from the contrast
after: Drink more water that day, unless your doctor limited you
The report is usually ready the same day
Discuss the result with your urologist
red_flags: Rash, itching, swelling of the face or trouble breathing - tell staff right away; at home, call your local emergency number
Pain or swelling at the injection site

faq.q: How is this different from a kidney CT?
faq.a: It is an X-ray with contrast. A CT is often done now, but sometimes the doctor chooses urography.

faq.q: What if I am allergic to iodine?
faq.a: Be sure to tell the doctor in advance. They will decide whether it can be done and whether preparation is needed.

reminders.text: Urography tomorrow. Take your creatinine test result. Eating: as the clinic said; ask your doctor about diabetes medicines.
